markers.impact: Reduced Adenosine Deaminase activity / elevated sleep pressure
markers.interpretation: ADA breaks down adenosine (the sleep-pressure molecule). The rs73598374 A allele reduces ADA activity. A-carriers accumulate adenosine slower but have higher baseline levels, leading to deeper sleep and more slow-wave activity, but potentially higher morning sleep inertia.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Actual sleep architecture is heavily impacted by circadian alignment, blue light exposure, and sleep hygiene.

sources.name: ADA genetic variant and human sleep EEG
sources.notes: Associates the G22A (rs73598374) variant with deeper slow-wave sleep in healthy individuals.

markers.impact: Circadian rhythm phase shifting / sleep fragmentation
markers.interpretation: PER2 is a core clock gene. The rs934945 A allele has been associated with sleep schedule disruptions, night awakenings, and anxious dreams in small clinical cohorts. A research-grade chronotype marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Research variant with low statistical power; does not override entrainment factors (light exposure, timing of food).

sources.name: PER2 clock gene variants and sleep phenotype
sources.notes: Analyzes correlation of PER2 variants with waking/sleeping chronotypes.

markers.impact: Altered circadian clock speed / eveningness preference
markers.interpretation: The CLOCK 3111C allele is robustly associated with eveningness chronotype ('night owl') and elevated sleep latency. Individuals carrying the C allele may experience delayed melatonin secretion onset.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Chronotype is highly plastic and entrains strongly to morning sunlight and meal times.

sources.name: CLOCK gene polymorphism and eveningness chronotype
sources.notes: Seminal study mapping 3111T>C to diurnal preference.

markers.impact: Reduced melatonin receptor density / impaired morning insulin release
markers.interpretation: MTNR1B rs10830963 G allele drives increased expression of melatonin receptors on pancreatic islet cells, causing prolonged inhibition of insulin secretion during the morning when melatonin is high. Explains circadian-metabolic glucose mismatch.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Suggests avoidance of high-carbohydrate meals immediately after waking or close to bedtime.

sources.name: MTNR1B and type 2 diabetes risk
sources.notes: Large GWAS identifying MTNR1B as a circadian regulator of pancreatic beta-cells.

markers.impact: Sleep homeostasis / morningness tendency / vulnerability to sleep loss
markers.interpretation: PER3 is not a simple SNP marker. The 5-repeat VNTR has been linked with stronger homeostatic sleep pressure, earlier sleep timing in some cohorts, and larger performance/cognitive changes under sleep restriction. Useful only if the raw source includes VNTR calling or if separately genotyped.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Most consumer raw DNA files do not include VNTRs; imputation from nearby SNPs is unreliable.

sources.name: PER3 VNTR and circadian/sleep phenotype review
sources.notes: Reviews PER3 VNTR links to delayed sleep phase and diurnal preference.

sources.name: Sleep quality, sleep structure, and PER3 genotype
sources.notes: Discusses PER3 VNTR as a candidate for chronotype and sleep homeostasis.

markers.impact: Familial delayed sleep phase / prolonged circadian period
markers.interpretation: Rare CRY1 splice-altering variant associated with delayed sleep phase patterns in families. Stronger than common chronotype SNPs when truly present, but usually absent from consumer SNP arrays.
do_not_claim: proof someone is a night owl
confirm_with: family history of delayed sleep phase
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Raw SNP arrays often miss rare splice variants; confirm with sequencing or a clinical-grade report.

sources.name: CRY1 mutation associated with delayed sleep phase disorder
sources.notes: Identifies a CRY1 splice variant associated with familial delayed sleep phase.

markers.impact: Morningness chronotype signal
markers.interpretation: RGS16 rs516134 is one of the replicated common chronotype markers associated with morningness. Its effect is small and should be interpreted as one point in a chronotype PRS, not as a standalone sleep identity.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Single chronotype SNPs explain tiny fractions of sleep timing; environment and light timing can override genotype.

sources.name: Genome-wide association analyses of chronotype in 697,828 individuals
sources.notes: Large chronotype GWAS; chronotype loci affect sleep timing more than sleep quality or duration.

markers.impact: Circadian timing / morningness signal
markers.interpretation: PER2 is a core circadian clock gene, and multiple PER2 variants have appeared in chronotype studies. Treat this as a small-effect timing marker that belongs in a PRS or locus-level module.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Effect allele orientation should be verified against the specific GWAS build before scoring.

sources.name: Chronotype GWAS in 128,266 individuals
sources.notes: Identified chronotype loci including circadian biology genes.

markers.impact: Familial natural short sleep phenotype
markers.interpretation: Rare DEC2/BHLHE41 mutation reported in familial natural short sleep. Carriers may naturally sleep fewer hours without typical impairment, but this requires phenotype confirmation. Do not confuse with sleep deprivation tolerance from stimulants or stress.
do_not_claim: proof that short sleep is healthy for all carriers
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Consumer raw DNA may not include or correctly call this rare variant; confirm with sequencing.

sources.name: Systematic review of natural short sleepers' genes
sources.notes: Reviews DEC2/BHLHE41 and other familial natural short sleep variants.

markers.impact: Familial natural short sleep / increased wakefulness
markers.interpretation: Rare ADRB1 mutation reported in familial natural short sleepers and modeled experimentally. Use as a rare-variant flag, not a consumer-SNP score.
do_not_claim: healthy sleep with any short duration
confirm_with: lifelong short sleep with preserved function
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Usually absent from raw SNP chips; requires rare-variant-aware sequencing.

sources.name: ADRB1 mutation and natural short sleep
sources.notes: Reports ADRB1 A187V in familial natural short sleep and functional modeling.

sources.name: Systematic review of natural short sleepers' genes
sources.notes: Summarizes ADRB1 as one of the human natural short sleep genes.

markers.impact: Familial natural short sleep / reduced sleep need
markers.interpretation: Rare NPSR1 variant associated with familial natural short sleep. NPSR1 is tied to arousal signaling, so this is mechanistically plausible but should be treated as a rare family-level finding.
do_not_claim: proof that sleeping little is harmless
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Not expected to be reliably present in ordinary consumer raw DNA files.

sources.name: NPSR1 mutation and natural short sleep
sources.notes: Reports NPSR1 Y206H associated with familial natural short sleep.

markers.variant_name: GRM1 familial natural short sleep rare variants
markers.impact: Glutamatergic natural short sleep signal
markers.interpretation: GRM1 rare variants have been reported in families with natural short sleep and are biologically relevant through glutamatergic signaling. Use gene-level rare-variant handling, not rsID scoring.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Requires exome/genome sequencing and variant interpretation; raw SNP files are insufficient.

sources.name: Systematic review of natural short sleepers' genes
sources.notes: Reviews GRM1 among familial natural short sleep genes.

markers.impact: Natural short sleep / sleep-need regulation
markers.interpretation: SIK3 N783Y has been reported as associated with human natural short sleep. This is a sleep-need regulator candidate and should be modeled as rare, high-impact when confirmed.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Requires sequencing; most direct-to-consumer raw DNA files will not contain this.

sources.name: SIK3-N783Y and human natural short sleep
sources.notes: Reports SIK3-N783Y association with natural short sleep.

markers.impact: Usual sleep duration / KATP-channel sleep regulation
markers.interpretation: ABCC9 rs11046205 was reported in a GWAS of sleep duration and has biological plausibility through KATP-channel regulation. Use as a small-effect duration marker, not a determinant of sleep need.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Effect size is population/context dependent; verify allele orientation before scoring.

sources.name: A KATP channel gene effect on sleep duration
sources.notes: Reports ABCC9 rs11046205 associated with sleep duration in European cohorts.

markers.impact: Longer usual sleep duration signal
markers.interpretation: The rs1823125 minor allele was associated with slightly longer usual sleep duration in CHARGE sleep-duration GWAS. The effect is minutes per allele, not hours.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Small effect; requires allele harmonization to the genotyping build and ancestry-aware interpretation.

sources.name: Novel loci associated with usual sleep duration
sources.notes: Reports rs1823125 minor allele associated with 3.1 minutes longer sleep duration per copy.

markers.impact: Small-effect sleep-duration signal
markers.interpretation: VRK2 loci were identified and replicated for usual sleep duration. Use as part of a polygenic duration module rather than a single actionable marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: The locus contains multiple signals; exact rsID/effect allele should be imported from a GWAS Catalog harmonized table before scoring.

sources.name: GWAS in 128,266 individuals identifies sleep-duration loci
sources.notes: Reports replicated sleep-duration associations at VRK2 with minute-scale effects.

markers.impact: Sleep intensity / slow-wave activity / sleep-dependent plasticity
markers.interpretation: BDNF Val66Met modulates activity-dependent BDNF secretion and has been associated with differences in NREM slow-wave activity and sleep-dependent learning. It belongs in a sleep-quality/neuroplasticity module, not a disorder module.
confirm_with: slow-wave sleep / delta power if available
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Effect is subtle, lab-measure dependent, and not usually visible from sleep-stage estimates produced by consumer wearables.

sources.name: BDNF Val66Met polymorphism modulates sleep intensity
sources.notes: Links BDNF Val66Met with human sleep slow-wave oscillations.

markers.impact: Insomnia symptoms signal with RLS/PLMS confounding
markers.interpretation: rs113851554 has been associated with insomnia symptoms in large GWAS, but MEIS1 is also a strong restless-legs/periodic-limb movement locus. In a sleep tool, this should trigger RLS/PLMS screening before interpreting it as primary insomnia.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Consumer raw DNA can capture the SNP, but phenotype overlap is a major limitation.

sources.name: GWAS of insomnia in 1,331,010 individuals
sources.notes: Identified 202 insomnia loci and implicated MEIS1 among many genes.

markers.impact: Caffeine-related sleep disruption / adenosine receptor sensitivity
markers.interpretation: ADORA2A rs5751876 influences sensitivity to caffeine's wakefulness-promoting effects and sleep disruption. Interpret only with caffeine timing and dose.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: The genotype matters most under caffeine exposure; no-caffeine nights may show little or no effect.

sources.name: ADORA2A genetic variation and caffeine/sleep
sources.notes: Reviews ADORA2A rs5751876 and caffeine-related sleep responses.

markers.impact: Caffeine clearance modifier affecting sleep timing risk
markers.interpretation: CYP1A2 rs762551 affects inducibility/caffeine metabolism in many pharmacogenetic models. For sleep, it is useful only combined with caffeine timing, ADORA2A sensitivity, smoking status, hormones, liver function, and dose.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: CYP1A2 interpretation has replication and context issues; recent studies challenge simplistic fast/slow claims.

sources.name: CYP1A2/ADORA2A caffeine pharmacogenetics review
sources.notes: Reviews complex relationships among CYP1A2, ADORA2A, caffeine behavior, and response.

markers.impact: Sleep-deprivation cognitive vulnerability / arousal regulation
markers.interpretation: COMT Val158Met can modulate dopamine tone and cognitive control under sleep deprivation. Include as a sleep-loss resilience/vulnerability modifier, not as a direct insomnia marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: COMT effects are pleiotropic and sex/context dependent; do not overinterpret a single SNP.

sources.name: COMT and cognitive control during sleep deprivation
sources.notes: Examines COMT genotype effects on cognitive control under sleep deprivation.

markers.impact: Narcolepsy type 1 susceptibility marker
markers.interpretation: HLA-DQB1*06:02 is strongly associated with narcolepsy, especially type 1 with cataplexy, but it is not causative by itself and is common in unaffected people. Treat as a triage flag requiring phenotype and clinical sleep testing.
do_not_claim: narcolepsy exclusion if absent in all cases
quantified risk from raw SNP alone
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Consumer SNP files often infer HLA poorly; confirm with HLA typing if clinically relevant.

sources.name: Narcolepsy HLA-DQB1*06:02 genotyping
sources.notes: Describes sensitivity/specificity limitations of HLA-DQB1*06:02 for narcolepsy.

sources.name: CMS MolDX HLA-DQB1*06:02 testing policy
sources.notes: States HLA-DQB1*06:02 typing is insufficient to confirm or rule out narcolepsy.

markers.impact: Autoimmune narcolepsy susceptibility locus
markers.interpretation: TCRA variants are associated with narcolepsy susceptibility and support an immune/T-cell component. Use as secondary risk context after HLA and symptoms.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Effect allele orientation must be harmonized; TCRA variants are small-effect compared with HLA-DQB1*06:02.

sources.name: TCRA association with narcolepsy
sources.notes: Reports T-cell receptor alpha locus association with narcolepsy.

markers.impact: Immune-cell survival / narcolepsy susceptibility
markers.interpretation: P2RY11 locus has been associated with narcolepsy and may relate to immune-cell signaling. It is a small-effect immune-genetics flag, not a standalone hypersomnia marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Allele orientation and linkage differ by ancestry/study; score only with harmonized GWAS data.

sources.name: P2RY11 and narcolepsy
sources.notes: Reports association near P2RY11 with narcolepsy.

markers.impact: Narcolepsy susceptibility in multiple ancestry cohorts
markers.interpretation: rs5770917 near CPT1B/CHKB has been associated with narcolepsy, originally strong in Japanese cohorts and seen in other ancestry analyses. Treat as a supporting marker only.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Effect size and transferability vary across populations; do not use without ancestry-aware interpretation.

sources.name: CPT1B/CHKB variant and narcolepsy
sources.notes: Reports rs5770917 near CPT1B/CHKB associated with narcolepsy.

markers.impact: Restless legs syndrome / periodic limb movement susceptibility
markers.interpretation: MEIS1 rs2300478 is a replicated RLS susceptibility marker. In sleep analysis, it matters because RLS/PLMS can masquerade as insomnia, fragmented sleep, hypersleep, or non-restorative sleep.
confirm_with: urge to move legs at rest
markers.raw_dna_limitation: RLS is clinical; genotype should trigger phenotype questions and iron status review.

sources.name: RLS variants in MEIS1, BTBD9, MAP2K5/SKOR1
sources.notes: Association study of known RLS GWAS loci.

markers.impact: Restless legs / periodic limb movement susceptibility
markers.interpretation: BTBD9 rs3923809 is associated with RLS/PLMS in multiple studies. Add to RLS/PLMS module and screen for sleep fragmentation, leg movement, and ferritin.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Association differs by ancestry and model; not deterministic.

sources.name: BTBD9 and RLS/PLMS association
sources.notes: Reports rs3923809 association with RLS in Korean cohorts.

sources.name: PLMS associated with BTBD9, MEIS1, MAP2K5/SKOR1, PTPRD
sources.notes: Links RLS/PLMS-related loci with periodic limb movements during sleep.

markers.impact: Restless legs syndrome susceptibility
markers.interpretation: rs9296249 in BTBD9 has been associated with RLS in Asian cohorts. Use as ancestry-aware secondary evidence in an RLS module.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Evidence is not equally strong across all ancestries; avoid universal scoring.

sources.name: BTBD9 RLS variants in Korean population
sources.notes: Reports rs9296249 association with RLS in Korean cohorts.

markers.impact: Restless legs syndrome susceptibility
markers.interpretation: The MAP2K5/SKOR1 region is a replicated RLS locus; later functional work prioritizes SKOR1 regulation. Treat this as part of the RLS/PLMS risk cluster.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Gene attribution is locus-level; effect allele should be harmonized in final PRS scoring.

sources.name: MEIS1-SKOR1 interaction and RLS locus
sources.notes: Functional study prioritizing SKOR1 in the MAP2K5/SKOR1 RLS region.

markers.impact: RLS/PLMS susceptibility and BTBD9 interaction
markers.interpretation: PTPRD variants have been associated with RLS/PLMS and may interact with BTBD9 in some cohorts. Use as a secondary modifier, not a primary flag.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Association and interaction effects need ancestry-aware replication; verify allele orientation.

sources.name: PLMS associated with PTPRD and other RLS loci
sources.notes: Reports PLMS associations involving PTPRD and established RLS genes.

markers.impact: Inflammation-linked obstructive sleep apnea susceptibility
markers.interpretation: TNF rs1800629 A has been reported as associated with OSA in meta-analyses, but the pre-GWAS literature is underpowered and heterogeneous. Treat as an inflammation/OSA susceptibility flag only.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: OSA is strongly phenotype/anatomy/body-composition dependent; genotype is not a substitute for sleep testing.

sources.name: Review of genetic association studies of obstructive sleep apnea
sources.notes: Field synopsis found TNFA rs1800629 associated with OSA but emphasized underpowered studies.

sources.name: TNF-α -308G/A polymorphism and OSA meta-analysis
sources.notes: 2023 meta-analysis suggests TNF-α -308A may be an OSA risk factor but calls for larger studies.

markers.impact: OSA risk mediated largely through adiposity/body composition
markers.interpretation: FTO rs8050136 has been associated with sleep apnea in PheWAS-type analyses, with attenuation after BMI adjustment. This is mostly an indirect body-composition pathway marker, not an airway marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Interpret through measured body composition; BMI adjustment attenuates much of the association.

sources.name: PheWAS showing FTO rs8050136 association with sleep apnea
sources.notes: Reports rs8050136 association with sleep apnea and attenuation after BMI adjustment.

markers.impact: OSA vulnerability via obesity/adiposity pathway
markers.interpretation: FTO rs9939609 is not a direct sleep-apnea SNP, but it can be included as an indirect obesity/adiposity risk marker because adiposity is a major OSA pathway.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Do not use as an OSA marker without phenotype and body-composition context.

sources.name: FTO rs8050136/obesity PheWAS and sleep apnea context
sources.notes: FTO associations with sleep apnea are attenuated after BMI adjustment; rs9939609 is included as an indirect adiposity-pathway proxy.

markers.impact: Sleep apnea symptoms signal
markers.interpretation: Rare/non-mainstream association reported for sleep-apnea symptoms. Include only as research-only until replicated in larger, clinically phenotyped cohorts.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Likely absent or unreliable in many raw files; phenotype definition may be symptom-based rather than PSG-confirmed OSA.

sources.name: Obstructive sleep apnea GWAS in Million Veteran Program
sources.notes: Large MVP GWAS underscores OSA genetic heterogeneity across sex and ancestry.

markers.variant_name: Obstructive sleep apnea polygenic risk score
markers.impact: Polygenic OSA liability: airway, adiposity, inflammation, craniofacial and metabolic pathways
markers.interpretation: OSA is better represented by a PRS plus phenotype stack than by single SNPs. The MVP GWAS supports ancestry/sex heterogeneity, so scoring should use ancestry-matched weights where available.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Requires GWAS summary statistics and ancestry-aware PRS; raw DNA alone is not enough.

sources.name: MVP obstructive sleep apnea GWAS
sources.notes: GWAS in 568,576 MVP participants; identifies heterogeneity by sex and ancestry.

markers.impact: NREM parasomnia susceptibility: sleepwalking / night terrors
markers.interpretation: HLA-DQB1*05:01 has been reported more often in sleepwalkers than controls, and sleepwalking/night terrors appear to share familial liability. Use as a parasomnia susceptibility flag only.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: HLA inference from consumer SNPs is weak; confirm with HLA typing if this matters clinically.

sources.name: HLA and genetic susceptibility to sleepwalking
sources.notes: Reports DQB1*0501 enrichment in sleepwalking.

sources.name: Hereditary factors in sleepwalking and night terrors
sources.notes: Supports shared genetic predisposition between sleepwalking and night terrors.

markers.impact: Familial sleepwalking susceptibility locus
markers.interpretation: A chromosome 20q12-q13.12 locus has been linked to sleepwalking in an extended family. This is not an rsID-ready consumer marker, but it belongs in a research module for familial NREM parasomnias.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Linkage locus requires family/genome analysis; not suitable for simple raw SNP scoring.

sources.name: First genetic locus for sleepwalking at chromosome 20q12-q13
sources.notes: Reports linkage in an extended family pedigree.

markers.impact: Nightmare liability overlapping insomnia and psychiatric traits
markers.interpretation: Recent GWAS work suggests nightmares have genetic overlap with insomnia and psychiatric traits, but no robust individual risk variant emerged in the 45,255-person GWAS. Use a PRS/trait-overlap module, not a single SNP.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: No clean consumer-SNP marker; this module needs PRS methods and phenotype context.

sources.name: Nightmares share genetic risk factors with sleep and psychiatric traits
sources.notes: GWAS in 45,255 individuals; nightmares share genetic background with sleep and psychiatric traits; no individual risk variants reported.

markers.impact: Dream affect / stress-related sleep disturbance candidate
markers.interpretation: Serotonin transporter variation has candidate-level links to stress reactivity and affective sleep phenomena. Include only as a low-confidence modifier for nightmares/vivid dreams under stress, never as a direct dream marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: 5-HTTLPR is poorly represented in ordinary raw SNP files and has a history of mixed candidate-gene replication.

sources.name: Nightmares share genetic risk factors with sleep and psychiatric traits
sources.notes: Use as a background rationale for overlap, not as direct 5-HTTLPR proof.

markers.impact: Stress/PTSD-related sleep disturbance and nightmare vulnerability candidate
markers.interpretation: FKBP5 rs1360780 is a stress-response/PTSD-adjacent marker. It may belong in a trauma-sleep/nightmare context module, but it is not a sleep-specific variant.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Epigenetics, trauma exposure, and current nervous-system state dominate interpretation; DNA alone is insufficient.

sources.name: Nightmare GWAS psychiatric/sleep overlap
sources.notes: Supports nightmares as genetically overlapping psychiatric/sleep traits; FKBP5 remains candidate-context only.

markers.impact: No robust single-SNP marker for lucid dreaming
markers.interpretation: Lucid dreaming is sleep-related, but current evidence does not support a robust single raw-DNA marker. Track phenotype behaviorally: dream recall, REM density, sleep fragmentation, meditation/training, and cholinergic/serotonergic medication context.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Do not score this from raw DNA until reliable GWAS or replicated variants exist.

sources.name: Nightmare GWAS as nearest sleep-dream genetics artifact
sources.notes: Dream-adjacent genetic evidence currently strongest for nightmare frequency/trait overlap, not lucid dreaming.

markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder susceptibility / alpha-synucleinopathy pathway
markers.interpretation: SNCA locus variants are associated with REM sleep behavior disorder. RBD is clinically important because dream enactment can precede Parkinsonian synucleinopathies, but genotype alone is not a diagnosis.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Single SNP effect is modest; RBD requires clinical phenotype and PSG confirmation.

sources.name: REM sleep behavior disorder GWAS
sources.notes: Identifies RBD risk loci near SNCA, GBA, TMEM175, INPP5F, and SCARB2.

markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder susceptibility / lysosomal pathway
markers.interpretation: GBA locus variants are among the strongest RBD genetic signals. Treat as a clinically meaningful flag only when dream enactment symptoms exist.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: GBA pathogenicity is variant-specific; GWAS markers are not the same as clinical GBA sequencing.

sources.name: RBD GWAS loci
sources.notes: Reports RBD loci including GBA.

markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder and synucleinopathy-related susceptibility
markers.interpretation: rs76763715 is a GBA variant/locus signal associated with RBD in GWAS Catalog evidence. It should trigger careful variant interpretation, not a casual consumer-genomics claim.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: GBA interpretation requires clinical variant nomenclature, zygosity, ancestry, and pathogenicity review.

sources.name: GWAS Catalog RBD association for rs76763715
sources.notes: Catalogs rs76763715 association with REM sleep behavior disorder.

markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder susceptibility
markers.interpretation: TMEM175 was identified as an RBD risk locus in GWAS. Include as a locus-level RBD/polygenic module marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Needs harmonized GWAS summary statistics before raw-DNA scoring.

sources.name: RBD GWAS
sources.notes: Reports RBD loci near SNCA, GBA, TMEM175, INPP5F, and SCARB2.

markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder susceptibility
markers.interpretation: INPP5F was identified as an RBD risk locus. Use as part of a PRS/locus panel, not as a standalone interpretation.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Locus-level marker needs exact harmonized variant import.

sources.name: RBD GWAS
sources.notes: Reports INPP5F among RBD loci.

markers.impact: REM sleep behavior disorder susceptibility
markers.interpretation: SCARB2 was identified as an RBD risk locus and biologically overlaps lysosomal pathways. Use as locus-level evidence in RBD module.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Requires exact GWAS harmonization for scoring.

sources.name: RBD GWAS
sources.notes: Reports SCARB2 among RBD loci.

markers.impact: Sleep bruxism genetic evidence remains weak/mixed
markers.interpretation: Sleep bruxism has reported candidate-gene studies, including serotonergic/dopaminergic genes, but evidence is mixed and not ready for consumer scoring. Keep as a research-gap panel unless a future GWAS produces robust loci.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Do not score from a handful of candidate SNPs; many bruxism cases are behavioral, medication-related, stress-related, or apnea-related.

sources.name: Scoping review of genetic polymorphisms in sleep bruxism
sources.notes: Summarizes candidate-gene literature and heterogeneity in sleep bruxism genetics.
